chapters.title: Thirteen cars, eight of them Ferraris
text: Thirteen LMGTE cars came to Austria: eight Ferrari 458 Italias, four Porsche 911 GT3 RSRs and a single Aston Martin Vantage. The Ferraris had set the pace in the first two rounds, to the irritation of rival teams and of LMP2 drivers who had to lap them, and the ACO responded by cutting the Ferrari engine restrictors by 1.3mm while leaving the Aston and the Porsches as they were.

The entry had its share of changes. Rob Bell returned to JMW’s #66 in place of Zampieri, Michael Meadows stood in at Gulf’s #86 Porsche because Ben Barker was racing the Supercup at Hockenheim, and Rugolo rejoined Cameron and Griffin in AF Corse’s #55. Richard Lietz joined the Felbermayrs in Proton’s #77 Porsche for his home race, and Christina Nielsen made her ELMS debut in IMSA Performance Matmut’s #76 alongside Narac and Armindo.

Bertolini’s #72 SMP Ferrari, which led the standings, was quickest in both Saturday practice sessions, with Griffin second in the afternoon. Cioci in the #54 AF Corse Ferrari was reprimanded after practice for improving his time under yellow flags.

chapters.title: Bertolini edges Lietz for pole
text: Bertolini took pole in the #72 on 1:29.286 and Lietz put the Proton Porsche #77 beside him on 1:29.499. Hall was third in Gulf’s #85 Aston Martin on 1:29.887, the Vantage’s best showing of the year, and Bell was less than a tenth behind in the #66. Kaffer’s #56 AT Racing Ferrari took fifth.
The #55 was only 12th in class, on 1:30.567, while the #86 Gulf Porsche of Carroll completed the thirteen-car field.

chapters.title: Brown sets the early pace
text: Brown started the Gulf Aston Martin and quickly pulled clear of the Ferraris, beginning a stint that put the #85 at the head of the class for the first half of the race. Cameron, starting the #55 from 12th in class, spent the opening laps working his way forward through the field.

chapters.title: Gulf fade, Kessel and AF Corse take over
text: Once Goethe took over from Brown the Aston Martin’s lead was eroded, and although Hall drove the final stint it never got back into podium contention. The race became a duel between Kessel’s #81 and the AF Corse #55, with the pit stops swapping the lead between them. Griffin made his mark by passing Kemenater in the penultimate hour, a clean move on the run to Turn 2, after which Griffin said Kemenater had defended fairly and he had given him room.

chapters.title: Rugolo passes Cressoni at Turn 1
text: Cressoni started the final hour with a decent lead for Kessel, but Rugolo had fresher tyres under him, planned his move and took the lead into Turn 1 with just over 30 minutes to go. The #55 stayed in front to the flag. Behind, Bell held off the charging AT Racing Ferrari of Kaffer for the last podium place, finishing under a second ahead.

chapters.title: AF Corse’s #55 wins as three Ferraris share the podium
text: The #55 won on 153 laps, with Kessel’s #81 and JMW’s #66 on the same lap. AT Racing’s #56, AF Corse’s #54 and the pole-sitting #72 were fourth to sixth, also on 153. Gulf’s #85 was seventh on 152, AF Corse’s #70 eighth on 151 and the #86 ninth on 149. The #58 and #77 followed on 149, and IMSA Performance Matmut’s #67 was 12th on 147. The #76 was not classified. The #55 also set the class fastest lap, 1:30.260.
Rugolo said Cressoni was on older tyres, which gave him time to plan the pass, and he called the car fantastic all race. The ELMS next goes to Paul Ricard on 13–14 September.

GTC.title: SMP Racing take GTC one-two as Formula Racing’s pole-sitter drops to 11th in class
GTC.dek: Ladygin, Basov and Persiani won in the #71 SMP Ferrari a lap ahead of the sister #73, with AF Corse’s #95 third; pole-sitting Formula Racing finished 11th in class.

facts.v: Jan Magnussen’s 1:30.647 in the Formula Racing Ferrari was 0.169s quicker than Korjus in the ART McLaren, who was second on the grid.

chapters.title: Twelve GT3 cars and a BoP shake-up
text: Twelve GTC cars started in Austria: seven Ferrari 458 Italia GT3s from SMP Racing, AF Corse, Team Sofrev-ASP and Formula Racing, two McLaren MP4-12Cs from ART Grand Prix, two Porsches and a Barwell-run BMW Z4. The BoP was reworked once more. The BMW lost 40kg, the Porsche 30kg, the Ferrari had its restrictors cut by 2mm and the McLaren’s turbo boost was adjusted.

Pro GT by Almeras changed its line-up, with Vaxivière and Hassid joining Perera in the #93 Porsche, and Prospeed’s #75 was confirmed as Van Splunteren, Vannelet and Parisy at the last moment. Team Russia by Barwell’s Cocker said the BMW still struggled for torque because of its weight.
Korjus put the ART McLaren #98 top of the first session on 1:31.272, then Kirill Ladygin led the afternoon in the #71 SMP Ferrari, with the Barwell BMW 0.223s adrift.

chapters.title: Magnussen puts Formula Racing on pole
text: Jan Magnussen took pole in the Formula Racing Ferrari #60 on 1:30.647, a second pole in a row for the Danish team after Imola. Korjus was second in ART’s #98 McLaren, 0.169s back. The next four cars, Sbirrazzuoli’s AF Corse #95, Beretta’s SMP #73, Ladygin’s #71 and Brundle’s ART #99, were covered by 0.163s and all within 0.5s of pole.

Perera’s Pro GT Porsche #93 was seventh, ahead of the Prospeed Porsche #75, the Barwell BMW #78 and the AF Corse Ferrari #63. Sofrev’s #59 and the SMP #57 of Rotenberg were last, the latter 5.3s off the pole time.

chapters.title: AF Corse lead briefly, Barwell BMW out
text: Sbirrazzuoli’s AF Corse #95 led briefly in the opening exchanges, but SMP Racing’s Ferraris soon took charge. The Barwell BMW #78 was out almost immediately and was not classified.

chapters.title: SMP take control
text: The #71 was the class of the field through the middle of the race, with strong stints from Persiani and Kirill Ladygin, backed by quick work in the pits. Persiani said the Michelin tyres were so good that they could triple-stint them without problems. The sister #73 of Beretta, Markozov and Anton Ladygin would finish a lap behind.

chapters.title: Persiani takes the flag a lap clear
text: The final hour was relatively serene for the #71 crew. Persiani took the chequered flag one lap ahead of the #73, which held second ahead of AF Corse’s #95 on the same lap.

chapters.title: SMP one-two; the pole-sitter 26 laps down
text: The #71 won on 151 laps, with the #73 and AF Corse’s #95 both on 150. ART’s #99 was fourth on 149 and the sister #98 fifth on 148, level with the Pro GT Porsche #93, AF Corse’s #63 and the Prospeed Porsche #75. SMP’s #57 was ninth on 147, Sofrev’s #59 tenth on 146, and the pole-sitting #60 finished 11th, 26 laps behind the winner on 125. The #78 was not classified. The #98 set the class fastest lap, 1:31.775.
Persiani said he was proud of the whole team after a perfect race in the pits. The ELMS next goes to Paul Ricard on 13–14 September.
